meta.title: "If you don't do it, everything will fall apart" — why your child fears the chain reaction | Sila Slova
meta.description: Teach your child to break down scary chain reactions step by step and check each one separately. Game-based course for children aged 8–12.

hero.headline: "You won't study — you'll fail everything, and nothing will work out!" — and your child is already scared?
hero.subheadline: One action — and straight to catastrophe. It sounds logical. But between the first step and "the end" there are layers of assumptions no one has checked.

media.alt: A child scared by a chain of events leading from one action to catastrophe

pain.title: "You won't go — you'll lose your chance forever" — that's not a forecast, it's a chain of assumptions
pain.body:
"You won't study — you'll get a bad grade, fail everything, nothing will work out". "You won't go — you'll miss your chance, and there'll never be another". At school, at home, in everyday conversations. One action gets inflated into a "catastrophe" through several steps. The child doesn't have time to check — they just get scared and agree.

This isn't panic or weakness. It's a natural response to exaggerated pressure: when the chain sounds coherent and confident, it's hard to stop and check each step. But every next link in such a chain is just an assumption — not a fact. And the further along, the less likely it becomes.

The result — fear drives the decision. "Better agree, just in case it really does all go that way" — and the child acts out of fear, not out of genuine reasoning.

faq.q: Is it a game or a learning course?
faq.a: Both at the same time. "Sila Slova" looks like a detective series, but every episode contains a hidden critical thinking lesson.

faq.q: What age is it suitable for?
faq.a: Ideal for 8–12 year olds. At this age, children are most receptive to new thinking patterns and haven't yet formed rigid biases.

faq.q: How much time is needed each day?
faq.a: 15–20 minutes per episode. Flexible schedule — your child can come back at any convenient time.

faq.q: Is registration required for the demo?
faq.a: No. The demo episode is fully open — no registration, no subscription, no personal data required.
